Kabul-Afghanistan.name: Kabul
Kabul-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Former Mughal subah seat elevated to Durrani imperial capital by Timur Shah in 1776; estimated at 50,000-60,000 (9,000-10,000 houses) by Elphinstone (1815), Burnes (1834) and Masson (1842), dipping after Pollock's 1842 sack of the Char Chatta bazaar and expanding under Abdur Rahman and Habibullah (Hensman 1881; Gregorian 1969; Adamec Vol. 6).

Kandahar-Afghanistan.name: Kandahar
Kandahar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Ahmad Shah Durrani's walled imperial capital (Ahmadshahi, founded 1761) peaked around 60,000 before declining after the 1776 capital move to Kabul; Masson (1830) counted 5,000 houses (25,000-30,000), Major Protheroe's 1880 census recorded 29,300, and Abdur Rahman's 1891 enumeration tallied 31,514 (Adamec Vol. 5; Noelle 1997).

Herat-Afghanistan.name: Herat
Herat-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Conolly (1830) and D'Arcy Todd recorded ~45,000 before the catastrophic 1837-38 Qajar siege reduced the city below 10,000; Ferrier (1845) documented recovery past 22,000, followed by the 1856 Persian siege, Dost Muhammad's 1863 conquest and steady recovery under Yate (1888) and Adamec Vol. 3.

Mazar-i-Sharif-Afghanistan.name: Mazar-i-Sharif
Mazar-i-Sharif-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Modest pilgrimage town around the Shrine of Ali during Burnes' 1832 visit that expanded rapidly after the 1866 Balkh cholera epidemic prompted transfer of the Afghan Turkestan capital; estimated at ~30,000 by Kostenko/Marvin (1878-79) and Adamec Vol. 4 (Lee 1996).

Tashkurghan-Afghanistan.name: Tashkurghan
Tashkurghan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Rebuilt as New Khulm after mid-18th-century destruction of Old Khulm, becoming the premier Bukhara-Kabul caravan entrepot of Afghan Turkestan; documented by Moorcroft (1825), Burnes (1834) and Yate (1886, 4,000-6,000 houses) in Adamec Vol. 4 and Lee (1996).

Maimana-Afghanistan.name: Maimana
Maimana-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Principal walled capital of the Uzbek Chahar Wilayat khanate; besieged and subjugated by Amir Abdur Rahman Khan in 1884, after which Yate and Peacocke (1885-86) counted ~3,000 intra-mural houses (~15,000 inhabitants) in Adamec Vol. 4 and Lee (1996).

Istalif-Afghanistan.name: Istalif
Istalif-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Prosperous Kohdaman Tajik horticultural and pottery town visited by Burnes and Masson (~14,000-15,000 before being sacked and burned by General McCaskill in September 1842), rebuilding to ~3,000 houses by the 1880s (Imperial Gazetteer; Adamec Vol. 6).

Ghazni-Afghanistan.name: Ghazni
Ghazni-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Strategic fortified town on the Kabul-Kandahar road; Masson (1832) and Vigne (1836) recorded ~1,000 houses inside the walled citadel (~5,000-6,000) with adjoining extramural suburbs and bazaar quarters bringing the agglomeration to 11,000-15,000 (Adamec Vol. 6).

Andkhoy-Afghanistan.name: Andkhoy
Andkhoy-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled Uzbek-Turkmen caravan khanate on the desert edge documented by Burnes (1834), Ferrier (1857) and Yate (1888); severely sacked by Yar Muhammad Khan of Herat in 1848 before recovering to ~13,000-15,000 urban/suburban inhabitants (Adamec Vol. 4; Lee 1996).

Sheberghan-Afghanistan.name: Sheberghan
Sheberghan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Capital of the semi-autonomous Uzbek Sheberghan Khanate; estimated at ~12,000 souls by Ferrier (c. 1845-56) and surveyed by Yate and Peacocke during the 1885-86 Afghan Boundary Commission (Adamec Vol. 4; Lee 1996).

Khanabad-Afghanistan.name: Khanabad
Khanabad-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Preferred healthier administrative and commercial capital of Qataghan-Kunduz; Wood (1838) estimated ~1,500 permanent houses plus seasonal bazaar households (~9,000-10,000), expanding as the walled Afghan provincial seat by 1914 (Adamec Vol. 1).

Charikar-Afghanistan.name: Charikar
Charikar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Flourishing Kohistan ironworking and trade town controlling the Hindu Kush passes; estimated at ~10,000 by Burnes (1834), temporarily disrupted during the 1841 Kohistan uprising and 1842 reprisals, and steady at 11,000-12,500 in Adamec Vol. 6.

Sar-e Pol-Afghanistan.name: Sar-e Pol
Sar-e Pol-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled Uzbek river-oasis khanate town south of Sheberghan containing Uzbek, Tajik, Hindu and Jewish merchant quarters; estimated at 8,000-11,000 by Ferrier (1857), Yate (1888) and Adamec Vol. 4 (Lee 1996).

Jalalabad-Afghanistan.name: Jalalabad
Jalalabad-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled Khyber-route winter town with a compact permanent core (~2,000-3,000 per Jenkyns 1879) plus extramural villages, Hindu merchant quarter and royal winter cantonments swelling to ~5,000-6,000 in the 19th century and ~10,000 under Amir Habibullah (Masson 1842; Adamec Vol. 6).

Kunduz-Afghanistan.name: Kunduz
Kunduz-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Marshland capital of Mir Murad Beg's Qataghan Uzbek khanate during Burnes (1832) and Wood (1838), temporarily swollen by deported Badakhshi populations before declining from malaria and Kabul annexation until Abdur Rahman's northern Pashtun settlement (Noelle 1997; Adamec Vol. 1).

Taluqan-Afghanistan.name: Taluqan
Taluqan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled Qataghan agricultural market town linking Kunduz and Badakhshan; documented by Wood (1841) and 1914 British intelligence summaries in Adamec Vol. 1 as a thriving mixed Uzbek-Tajik bazaar center of ~1,500-1,900 houses.

Gardez-Afghanistan.name: Gardez
Gardez-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Historic Bala Hisar citadel and administrative market center of Zurmat/Paktia surrounded by clustered Tajik and Ghilzai villages; assessed from 19th-century British frontier itineraries and Adamec Vol. 6.

Paghman-Afghanistan.name: Paghman
Paghman-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fertile Kohdaman piedmont orchard agglomeration northwest of Kabul noted by Masson (1842) and expanded as a royal summer retreat under Amirs Abdur Rahman and Habibullah (Gregorian 1969; Adamec Vol. 6).

Faizabad-Afghanistan.name: Faizabad
Faizabad-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Capital of Badakhshan on the Kokcha River; severely depopulated by Murad Beg's 1829-32 deportations witnessed by Wood (1838) before rebuilding under Mir Shah and Afghan provincial administration (Elias 1886; Adamec Vol. 1).

Aqcha-Afghanistan.name: Aqcha
Aqcha-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Irrigated Uzbek-Turkmen khanate estimated at 7,000-8,000 by Ferrier (1845) before devastating decline from Ishak Khan's 1869 revolt, 1886-87 famine and abandonment to barely 300-400 inhabited urban houses around 1900 (Yate 1888; Adamec Vol. 4).

Farah-Afghanistan.name: Farah
Farah-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Ancient walled fortress town on the Farah Rud contested between Herat and Kandahar; Ferrier (1845) noted decayed ramparts and sparse mud dwellings inside its vast perimeter, stabilizing at 6,000-7,500 by 1914 (Adamec Vol. 2).

Aybak-Afghanistan.name: Aybak
Aybak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified Samangan river-valley khanate and Hindu Kush caravan waystation south of Tashkurghan; documented by Burnes (1834) and late-19th-century surveys at ~1,200-1,500 households (Adamec Vol. 4).

Balkh-Afghanistan.name: Balkh
Balkh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Severely ruined former metropolis besieged by Shah Murad of Bukhara (1793), estimated at ~2,000 by Burnes (1832), devastated by cholera in 1866 when the capital shifted to Mazar-i-Sharif, and counted at ~600 permanent families (~3,000) in 1886 (Peacocke; Lee 1996; Adamec Vol. 4).

Nijrab-Afghanistan.name: Nijrab
Nijrab-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Densely settled Tajik and Pashai Kohistan mountain valley hub composed of clustered fortified villages and bazaars noted by Masson (1842) and British frontier surveys (Adamec Vol. 6).

Rustaq-Afghanistan.name: Rustaq
Rustaq-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Prosperous Uzbek-Tajik agricultural and cotton-trading town north of Taluqan on the Badakhshan approaches; recorded by Wood (1841), Elias (1886) and Adamec Vol. 1.

Sabzawar-Afghanistan.name: Sabzawar
Sabzawar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled caravan town on the Herat-Farah road; 19th-century British and French accounts (Ferrier 1857; Adamec Vol. 3) recorded ~1,000 inhabited mud houses (~5,000) within its ramparts plus adjacent Nurzai villages.

Baraki Barak-Afghanistan.name: Baraki Barak
Baraki Barak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Principal Logar Valley administrative hub and historical center of the Ormur (Baraki) community surrounded by irrigated qalas; documented by Leech (1838), Masson (1842) and Adamec Vol. 6.

Girishk-Afghanistan.name: Girishk
Girishk-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Strategic Barakzai fort and toll-crossing commanding the Helmand River on the Kandahar-Herat trunk road; assessed from Ferrier (1857), Second Anglo-Afghan War itineraries and Adamec Vol. 5.

Ghorian-Afghanistan.name: Ghorian
Ghorian-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Western frontier fortress town of Herat contested during the 1837 and 1856 Persian invasions; late-19th-century British intelligence records cited ~1,140 resident families (~5,700) in Adamec Vol. 3.

Khost-Afghanistan.name: Khost
Khost-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Matun fort and central bazaar hub of the fertile Khost valley inhabited by Khostwal and Mangal Pashtuns; surveyed by British expeditions in 1879-80 and detailed in Adamec Vol. 6.

Qala-i Naw-Afghanistan.name: Qala-i Naw
Qala-i Naw-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified administrative seat of Badghis serving Qala-i Naw Hazara and Jamshidi Aimaq communities; mapped and counted during the 1884-86 Afghan Boundary Commission (Yate 1888; Adamec Vol. 3).

Kalat-i Ghilzai-Afghanistan.name: Kalat-i Ghilzai
Kalat-i Ghilzai-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Formidable hilltop fortress and Tokhi Ghilzai administrative center on the Kandahar-Ghazni road; documented during the 1842 British garrison defence, 1880 campaign and Adamec Vol. 5.

Baghlan-Afghanistan.name: Baghlan
Baghlan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Agrarian Uzbek-Tajik river-valley town in Qataghan prior to 20th-century industrial sugar/cotton expansion; assessed from 19th-century Qataghan itineraries and Adamec Vol. 1.

Mehtarlam-Afghanistan.name: Mehtarlam
Mehtarlam-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Shrine and agricultural district center of the irrigated Laghman valley between Alishing and Alingar rivers; assessed from Masson (1842) and Adamec Vol. 6.

Behsud-Afghanistan.name: Behsud
Behsud-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Eastern Hazarajat highland center noted by Moorcroft (1825) and Muhammad Hussain Khan; suffered severe demographic contraction during Amir Abdur Rahman's 1891-93 Hazara War and pasture transfers to Kuchi nomads (Kakar 1979; Adamec Vol. 6).

Pul-e Alam-Afghanistan.name: Pul-e Alam
Pul-e Alam-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: River crossing and provisioning hub in central Logar along the Kabul-Gardez military and trade highway; documented in 19th-century British route books and Adamec Vol. 6.

Bamyan-Afghanistan.name: Bamyan
Bamyan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Hindu Kush caravan valley and cave-fortified Hazara/Tajik gateway visited by Moorcroft, Burnes (1832) and Masson (1835), dipping briefly during the 1891-93 Hazarajat campaigns before stabilizing under Kabul's garrison (Adamec Vol. 6).

Panjab-Afghanistan.name: Panjab
Panjab-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: High Koh-i Baba valley stronghold of the Dai Zangi Hazaras; assessed from Muhammad Hussain Khan's Report on the Hazarajat and Kakar (1979), reflecting sharp depopulation during the 1891-93 Hazara War.

Chakhansur-Afghanistan.name: Chakhansur
Chakhansur-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified capital of the Sanjarani Baluch chiefs in Afghan Sistan prior to 20th-century Zaranj urbanization; documented by the Goldsmid (1872) and McMahon (1903-05) Sistan Boundary Commissions and Adamec Vol. 2.

Lalpura-Afghanistan.name: Lalpura
Lalpura-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Seat of the Mohmand Khanate commanding the Kabul River gorge and northern Khyber approaches; documented in Elphinstone (1815), Second Anglo-Afghan War frontier intelligence and Adamec Vol. 6.

Jaghori-Afghanistan.name: Jaghori
Jaghori-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fertile southern Hazarajat valley oasis anchored on Sang-i Masha; spared the worst devastation of the 1891-93 Hazara War through early negotiated submission (Kakar 1979; Adamec Vol. 6).

Tarinkot-Afghanistan.name: Tarinkot
Tarinkot-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Upper Helmand Durrani-Hazara frontier hub in Uruzgan that expanded after 1893 as Amir Abdur Rahman resettled Popalzai and Barakzai clans onto former Uruzgani Hazara lands (Kakar 1979; Adamec Vol. 5).

Sangcharak-Afghanistan.name: Sangcharak
Sangcharak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Well-watered Uzbek-Tajik river-valley chiefdom centered on Tukzar south of Sar-e Pol, incorporated into Afghan Turkestan under Abdur Rahman Khan (Yate 1888; Adamec Vol. 4).

Karukh-Afghanistan.name: Karukh
Karukh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Prosperous vineyard and orchard market town northeast of Herat documented in 1885-86 Afghan Boundary Commission route itineraries and Adamec Vol. 3.

Andarab-Afghanistan.name: Andarab
Andarab-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Northern Hindu Kush Tajik valley hub guarding the Khawak Pass road between Panjshir and Qataghan; described by Burnes (1834), Wood (1841) and Adamec Vol. 1.

Bazarak-Afghanistan.name: Bazarak
Bazarak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Central market cluster of the populous Tajik Panjshir Valley supporting irrigated terracing, ironworking and trans-Hindu Kush transit (Burnes 1834; Masson 1842; Adamec Vol. 6).

Yakawlang-Afghanistan.name: Yakawlang
Yakawlang-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fertile northern Hazarajat valley provisioning district on the Band-i Amir headwaters; documented in Muhammad Hussain Khan's survey and Adamec Vol. 4/6, showing contraction after the 1891-93 Hazara War.

Musa Qala-Afghanistan.name: Musa Qala
Musa Qala-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified Alizai Durrani oasis and regional market in northern Zamindawar along the Musa Qala river (Elphinstone 1815; Adamec Vol. 5).

Jurm-Afghanistan.name: Jurm
Jurm-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Well-watered Kokcha valley fortress town that served as alternate capital of the Mirs of Badakhshan during Faizabad's 1830s devastation (Wood 1841; Elias 1886; Adamec Vol. 1).

Obeh-Afghanistan.name: Obeh
Obeh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Upper Hari Rud valley district center east of Herat surveyed in Muhammad Takki Khan's Persian administrative report on Herat province and Adamec Vol. 3.

Daulatabad-Afghanistan.name: Daulatabad
Daulatabad-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified Faryab/Shirin Tagab oasis linking Maimana and Andkhoy within the Uzbek Chahar Wilayat; documented by Yate (1888) and Adamec Vol. 4 (Lee 1996).

Urgun-Afghanistan.name: Urgun
Urgun-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Southeastern Sulaiman frontier trading basin inhabited by Tajik-Farsiwan artisans and Kharoti/Wazir Pashtuns along the Gomal caravan routes (Broadfoot 1885; Adamec Vol. 6).

Panjwai-Afghanistan.name: Panjwai
Panjwai-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Irrigated Arghandab vineyard and market center west of Kandahar serving Nurzai and Ishaqzai Durrani agrarian districts (Elphinstone 1815; Adamec Vol. 5).

Asadabad-Afghanistan.name: Asadabad
Asadabad-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Kunar-Pech river confluence settlement (historically Chigha Sarai / Kunar khanate center) controlling fertile rice valleys and routes into Kafiristan and Chitral (Adamec Vol. 6).

Chaghcharan-Afghanistan.name: Chaghcharan
Chaghcharan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Upper Hari Rud valley hub of the Firozkohi Aimaqs in Ghor, serving as seasonal administrative and bazaar node along the Herat-Kabul central highland track (Ferrier 1857; Adamec Vol. 3).

Mukur-Afghanistan.name: Mukur
Mukur-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified Taraki Ghilzai waystation and Tarnak headwaters oasis on the Ghazni-Qalat high road; noted in British campaign route books (1839-80) and Adamec Vol. 6.

Nili-Afghanistan.name: Nili
Nili-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Central valley cluster of the autonomous Dai Kundi Hazara confederation documented in Muhammad Hussain Khan's Report on the Hazarajat; suffered severe population losses during Amir Abdur Rahman's 1891-93 campaigns (Kakar 1979).

Bagram-Afghanistan.name: Bagram
Bagram-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Shomali Plain agricultural village cluster adjacent to ancient Kapisa mounds explored by Masson (1833-37); assessed from Kohistan revenue and village surveys in Adamec Vol. 6.

Kishm-Afghanistan.name: Kishm
Kishm-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Lower Badakhshan orchard valley and fortified town guarding the Taluqan-Faizabad road; documented by Wood (1841), Elias (1886) and Adamec Vol. 1.

Anardara-Afghanistan.name: Anardara
Anardara-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Compact fortified Tajik-Kakuri pomegranate oasis and pass town northwest of Farah; described by Ferrier (1857) and Adamec Vol. 2, with brief 1890s tax-revolt emigration under Abdur Rahman.

Bala Murghab-Afghanistan.name: Bala Murghab
Bala Murghab-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Murghab valley frontier fort and oasis garrisoned heavily after the 1885 Panjdeh crisis; surveyed in detail by Maitland and Yate (1888) and Adamec Vol. 3.

Lash-i Juwayn-Afghanistan.name: Lash-i Juwayn
Lash-i Juwayn-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Contested mud-brick citadel and border settlement on the lower Farah Rud between Farah and Sistan; recorded by Ferrier (1857), Goldsmid (1872) and Adamec Vol. 2.

Sharan-Afghanistan.name: Sharan
Sharan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Katawaz plateau fortified market center of the Sulaimankhel Ghilzais linking Ghazni to Urgun and the Gomal pass; assessed from British frontier itineraries and Adamec Vol. 6.

Maruf-Afghanistan.name: Maruf
Maruf-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Ancestral Barakzai Durrani upland settlement and fortified valley east of Kandahar on the Arghastan headwaters (Elphinstone 1815; Adamec Vol. 5).

Malistan-Afghanistan.name: Malistan
Malistan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Central Hazarajat highland settlement cluster west of Jaghori; assessed from Muhammad Hussain Khan's survey and Kakar (1979), reflecting 1891-93 Hazara War losses and partial recovery.

Kushk-Afghanistan.name: Kushk
Kushk-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Jamshidi Aimaq frontier stronghold north of Herat on the Kushk River commanding the approach toward Merv and Russian Turkestan (Yate 1888; Adamec Vol. 3).

Lal wa Sarjangal-Afghanistan.name: Lal wa Sarjangal
Lal wa Sarjangal-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: High-altitude Dai Zangi Hazara valley cluster on the upper Hari Rud headwaters; suffered sharp demographic loss during the 1891-93 Hazara War (Muhammad Hussain Khan; Kakar 1979; Adamec Vol. 3).

Kamdesh-Afghanistan.name: Kamdesh
Kamdesh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Chief tiered-cliff stronghold of the Kam Kafirs in the Bashgal Valley; G.S. Robertson (1889-91) counted 500-600 houses (~3,000 inhabitants) shortly before Amir Abdur Rahman's 1896 conquest and forced Islamisation of Kafiristan/Nuristan (Gregorian 1969; Adamec Vol. 6).

Parun-Afghanistan.name: Parun
Parun-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Sacred central valley cluster of six fortified Presun villages in Kafiristan visited by Robertson (1896), reduced by combat, deportations and flight during the 1896 conquest of Nuristan before gradual recovery (Adamec Vol. 6).

Spin Boldak-Afghanistan.name: Spin Boldak
Spin Boldak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Unsettled Achakzai steppe prior to Amir Abdur Rahman's construction of the frontier fort Qala-i Jadid c. 1890 opposite the British Chaman railhead; grew modestly as a customs and garrison post through 1919 (Adamec Vol. 5).

Ishkashim-Afghanistan.name: Ishkashim
Ishkashim-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: High-altitude Pamir border settlement along the Panj River guarding the gateway to Wakhan; estimated at ~1,200 souls by Wood (1841), Ney Elias (1886) and Adamec Vol. 1.

Ze Nowroz Ya Shah Wa Haros-Afghanistan.name: Ze Nowroz Ya Shah Wa Haros
